image_description: A close-up, high-angle shot of a European fire salamander (Salamandra salamandra) resting on dark, textured ground (likely soil or leaf litter). The salamander has a glossy black body with distinct, irregular bright yellow spots. Its skin appears wet and reflective. The head is visible on the left, showing a small dark eye. The limbs are short and partially obscured by the angle and ground texture. The tail extends towards the right, tapering off.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head shape appears somewhat generic and lacks the distinct, swollen parotoid glands characteristic of the species. The transition from neck to head is smooth rather than showing the specific glandular bulges.

The body shape is consistent with a robust, cylindrical salamander form.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The color pattern matches the species description well, with high-contrast yellow spots on a black background.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The limbs are heavily occluded by the body angle and blend into the dark background. Individual digits are not clearly resolvable to count or verify morphology.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail extends out of the frame or fades into the background blur before the tip is visible, making it impossible to verify the rounded tip or exact length ratio.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The yellow spots have a slightly 'painted-on' or matte texture that contrasts unnaturally with the highly glossy black skin. They lack the subtle integration into the skin surface seen in real specimens.

The front left limb appears to merge indistinctly with the ground and the body. There is no clear separation of the upper arm from the torso, suggesting a melting or fusion artifact common in AI generation.
The ground texture (twigs/leaves) has inconsistent focus and scale, appearing somewhat warped around the subject's edges, indicating slight boundary bleeding.
